bio: Bradford Scott Lander (born July 8, 1969) is an American politician and urban planner who is the U.S. Representative-elect for New York's 10th congressional district. A progressive Democrat, he previously served as New York City comptroller from 2022 until 2025, and before that served on the New York City Council from 2010 to 2021, representing the 39th district, which is partly based in Brooklyn.
offices: Member of the New York City Council (2010–2021)

items.t: Called for ending the 421a tax incentive program for developers of market-rate apartments (2022).
items.q: In 2022, Lander called for ending 421a, a program that provided tax incentives for developers of market-rate apartments who also added below-market rentals.

items.t: Supported defunding the police by cutting its budget by $1 billion (2020).
items.q: Lander voiced support for defunding the police and limiting police powers by cutting their budget by $1 billion in 2020.

items.t: Linked arms with an immigrant defendant at immigration court in June 2025 and was arrested and handcuffed by ICE officials.
items.q: Lander was arrested and handcuffed by masked Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials at an immigration court while linking arms with a person ICE was trying to detain.

items.t: Began accompanying defendants to immigration hearings as deportations increased (2025).
items.q: In June 2025, as Donald Trump increased deportations of immigrants, Lander began accompanying defendants to immigration hearings.

items.t: Called on Mayor Adams to abandon the shift of retired municipal workers onto a new Medicare program (2022).
items.q: In March 2022, Lander called on Mayor Eric Adams to abandon his effort to shift retired municipal workers onto a new Medicare program and comply with a court order declaring the move illegal.

items.t: Refused to register the city's contract with Aetna for the Medicare program (2022).
items.q: He subsequently refused to register the city's contract with Aetna, citing pending legislation that called the program's legality into question

items.t: Led the push to secure air conditioning for all New York City public school classrooms.
items.q: Lander led the push to secure air conditioning for all New York City Public Schools classrooms, shining a spotlight on the 25 percent of classrooms that lacked it.

items.t: Urged suspending criminal arrests, summonses and warrant enforcement for low-level offenses and releasing most Rikers Island inmates over 50 (2020).
items.q: Lander urged that the police suspend criminal arrests, summonses, warrant enforcement, and parole violations for low-level offenses, and release most of the over 900 people incarcerated at Rikers Island who were over 50 years old.

items.t: Called for disbanding the NYPD Vice Unit and decriminalizing prostitution (2020).
items.q: In December 2020, he called for the disbandment of the New York City Police Department Vice Unit and for decriminalizing prostitution.

items.t: Said he would vote to recognize a Palestinian state and oppose sales of offensive weapons to Israel if elected (2025).
items.q: Lander said that if elected, he would vote to recognize a Palestinian state and oppose the sale of offensive weapons to Israel.

items.t: Wrote in Haaretz urging President Biden to stop providing a "blank check" to the Israeli government (2023).
items.q: urging President Joe Biden and Secretary of State Antony Blinken to stop providing a " blank check " to an "increasingly authoritarian" Israeli government

items.t: Was against the censure of Rep. Rashida Tlaib and called for Rep. Randy Fine to be censured.
items.q: Lander also strongly opposed the censure of U.S. Representative Rashida Tlaib while calling for U.S. Representative Randy Fine to be censured

items.t: Supports conditioning U.S. military aid to Israel and has called Israel's war in Gaza a genocide.
items.q: a liberal Zionist who has called Israel's war in Gaza a genocide and supports conditioning military aid" to Israel

items.t: Supported removing the Christopher Columbus statue from Columbus Circle.
items.q: He supported removing the statue of Christopher Columbus from Columbus Circle.

items.t: Helped pass paid sick leave over Mayor Bloomberg's veto (2013).
items.q: In 2013, Lander played a key role in a campaign to pass paid sick leave over Mayor Bloomberg's veto

items.t: Passed legislation requiring fast food and retail companies to give workers stable scheduling (2017).
items.q: In 2017, he passed legislation to require fast food and retail companies to give their workers stable scheduling and restrict on-call scheduling and last-minute changes.

items.t: Sponsored a bill preventing fast food workers from being fired without just cause.
items.q: Lander also sponsored a successful bill to prevent fast food workers from being fired without just cause and to allow them to appeal terminations through arbitration.

items.t: Passed legislation banning discriminatory employment credit checks (2015).
items.q: In 2015, Lander passed legislation to ban discriminatory employment credit checks.

items.t: Worked to create a Certificate of No Harassment program protecting tenants from harassment and displacement (2017).
items.q: Lander worked with advocates at the Association of Neighborhood and Housing Development and Make the Road New York to create a Certificate of No Harassment program

items.t: Was a leading advocate of moving homeless people into vacant New York City hotel rooms during the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.q: Lander has been a leading advocate of a program that has moved over 9,500 homeless people (his goal is 30,000) to vacant New York City hotel rooms

items.t: Was against rezoning the Long Island College Hospital site to include affordable housing.
items.q: Lander opposed rezoning the site of Long Island College Hospital to include affordable housing.

items.t: Helped bring participatory budgeting to New York City, letting citizens propose and vote on municipal budget items.
items.q: Lander was one of four Council members who brought participatory budgeting to New York City, which allows citizens to propose, develop, and vote on items in the municipal budget.
